haiku-low.q1: Durable when the caller's transaction commits and inserts the monolith row. If that transaction fails, no row exists.
haiku-low.q2: It redelivers the message if not acknowledged within 30 seconds, possibly to another consumer.
haiku-low.q3: Five attempts, waiting 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2 to 5. Then the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: One at a time: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset. Each runs at least 3 days; order_confirmed's p99 must be under 60 s first.
haiku-low.q5: The notification id, always passed. MailRelay drops a repeat with the same key within 24 hours and returns success.
haiku-low.q6: The outbox relay publishes it to broker topic notifications.requested, then sets published_at once the broker confirms. The monolith is done then.
haiku-low.q7: The enqueue step, via enqueue_notification, reads flag notify.route.<type> when the row is created, in the caller's transaction.
haiku-low.q8: The consumer finds the existing deliveries id, skips the insert and acknowledges. Also, deliveries is unique on id, and MailRelay drops repeated keys.
haiku-low.q9: Only after committing the deliveries row, before sending. A crash before the commit means redelivery after 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: In the service's deliveries table (attempts, next_attempt_at, status). The sender polling loop claims due pending rows and applies retry policy.
haiku-low.q11: They finish on the service, not the old worker. The service must keep running until they are done. Nothing is lost or sent twice.
haiku-low.q12: Per the consumer step, id, type, email, payload and created time are stored from the message. The service's sender renders the template.

sonnet.q1: When the caller's transaction commits, the row is inserted into the monolith notifications table (as pending). Whether it exists depends on that transaction: if it fails, no row exists and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: It redelivers the message after 30 s, possibly to another consumer (at-least-once).
sonnet.q3: 5 attempts total, with waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2 to 5. Then the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: One type at a time: shipping_update first (at least 3 days), then order_confirmed (at least 3 days), then password_reset last. Before password_reset moves, order_confirmed's p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay must be under 60 s.
sonnet.q5: The idempotency key, which is the notification id. If MailRelay accepted a send with the same key in the last 24 hours, it drops the new one and returns success.
sonnet.q6: The outbox relay in the monolith claims route='service' rows with empty published_at (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and publishes them to the broker topic notifications.requested; the service's consumer receives them. The monolith's part is done when the broker confirms storage and published_at is set.
sonnet.q7: The enqueue step (enqueue_notification) in the monolith decides, reading the per-type flag notify.route.<type> and writing route (monolith or service) into the row at enqueue time, in the caller's transaction. It is set once.
sonnet.q8: The consumer finds the existing deliveries id (unique on notification id), skips the insert and acknowledges. Also MailRelay drops repeated idempotency keys.
sonnet.q9: It acknowledges only after inserting the deliveries row and committing, and before any sending (the sender sends later). If it crashes before the commit, the broker redelivers after 30 s. Crash between commit and ack is not explicitly stated, though a redelivery would hit the existing id and be acknowledged.
sonnet.q10: In the service database deliveries table (status, attempts, next_attempt_at). The sender polling loop on the service instances acts on it.
sonnet.q11: Rows already routed to the service finish there; nothing is lost or sent twice. The service must keep running until they are done. They are not sent by the old worker. If the service is broken at that time, they wait until it recovers, which is not handled.
sonnet.q12: Per notification: id, type, email and payload (plus original created time). The email content is rendered by the service's sender from the template.
